boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten named UM-Dearborn study environments, from quiet library floors to outdoor seating and collaborative campus spaces.

cards.title: CASL Atrium
cards.subtitle: College of Arts, Sciences, and Letters
cards.notes: Set up beneath the atrium’s floor-to-ceiling windows when you want varied seating and natural light for an on-campus work session.
cards.short_summary: A central, light-filled CASL setting with varied seating.
cards.evidence_claim: UM-Dearborn identifies the CASL Atrium as a social study space with varied seating and floor-to-ceiling windows.
cards.access_notes: Located in the center of the CASL building, according to the university source.

cards.title: Language Lab
cards.subtitle: Third level, CASL
cards.notes: Bring individual work or a small project to this CASL lab, using its computers, screens, projectors, and charging stations.
cards.short_summary: A technology-equipped CASL space for individual or shared work.
cards.evidence_claim: The university says the Language Lab is on CASL’s third level and has computers, TV screens, projectors, charging stations, and language tutors.
cards.access_notes: Located on the third level of CASL; the cited page describes individual and group work use.

cards.title: Mardigian Library Floors 1 and 2
cards.subtitle: Mardigian Library
cards.notes: Use the second floor’s cozy seating, movable charging stations, meeting rooms, computer station, and whiteboards to shape your session.
cards.short_summary: Library floors combining collaboration areas, computing, and flexible study tools.
cards.evidence_claim: UM-Dearborn states that the library’s second floor has study areas, movable charging stations, meeting rooms, a computer station, and whiteboards.
cards.access_notes: Public collaboration areas are on the first and second floors; ITS computer labs there are open to all UM-Dearborn students.

cards.title: Mardigian Library Floors 3 and 4
cards.subtitle: Mardigian Library
cards.notes: Choose an upper-floor desk when you need a quieter setting and want to separate focused reading or writing from social activity.
cards.short_summary: Quieter upper library floors with desks intended for concentrated work.
cards.evidence_claim: The university describes Mardigian Library’s third and fourth floors as quieter study space with desks for focus and concentration.
cards.access_notes: The cited university page identifies these as the library’s third- and fourth-floor study areas.

cards.title: Wolverine Commons
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Renick University Center
cards.notes: Use the second-floor commons when you need seating options that can accommodate either solo coursework or a planned group meeting.
cards.short_summary: A flexible-seating study area in the renovated Renick University Center.
cards.evidence_claim: UM-Dearborn identifies Wolverine Commons on the RUC’s second floor as a study area with varied seating for individual or group work.
cards.access_notes: Located on the second floor of the Renick University Center, according to the cited page.

cards.title: RUC Newly Renovated Lounge
cards.subtitle: Renick University Center
cards.notes: Pick a couch for independent reading or use the study booths for a small working session in the RUC’s renovated lounge.
cards.short_summary: A renovated RUC lounge with couches, study booths, and updated seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The university says the RUC’s renovated lounge includes couches, study booths, a fireplace, and updated seating.
cards.access_notes: The cited university page places this study lounge in the Renick University Center.

cards.title: Natural Science Building Study Areas
cards.subtitle: Natural Science Building
cards.notes: Walk the building’s three floors to find seating with scenic views, then use the available whiteboards, markers, and charging stations.
cards.short_summary: Three-floor study areas with seating, scenic views, whiteboards, and charging.
cards.evidence_claim: UM-Dearborn states that the Natural Science Building’s study areas include whiteboards, markers, charging stations, seating, and some scenic views.
cards.access_notes: Located at the south end of campus; the university source describes study areas across all three floors.

cards.entity_name: Tony England Engineering Lab Building Study Areas
cards.title: Tony England Engineering Lab Building Study Areas
cards.subtitle: Tony England Engineering Lab Building
cards.notes: Use the building’s large-window seating or enclosed lounge areas, and keep whiteboards nearby for a project-focused working block.
cards.short_summary: Engineering-building spaces combining daylight, whiteboards, and enclosed lounges.
cards.evidence_claim: The university describes study areas in the Tony England Engineering Lab Building with large windows, lighting, whiteboards, and enclosed lounges.
cards.access_notes: The cited university page identifies study areas within the Tony England Engineering Lab Building.

cards.title: RUC Patio
cards.subtitle: Behind the Renick University Center
cards.notes: When weather permits, take reading or laptop work to the patio behind the RUC and use its outdoor seating near CASL.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor RUC study option with landscape and seating.
cards.evidence_claim: UM-Dearborn identifies the patio behind the RUC as an outdoor study location with landscape and a wide selection of seating.
cards.access_notes: Located behind the RUC; the source frames it as an option during warmer months.

cards.title: Chancellor’s Pond
cards.subtitle: UM-Dearborn campus
cards.notes: Bring a book or quiet reading task to the chairs and stone benches beside the pond when the outdoor setting is in season.
cards.short_summary: A pond-side outdoor reading and study setting with seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The university says Chancellor’s Pond has a spring fountain, yellow chairs, and stone benches suitable for reading or studying.
cards.access_notes: The cited page describes this as an outdoor option during non-winter months.
